assignments.note: 2018-05 AI safety via debate
assignments.why: Proposes a zero-sum debate between two agents judged by a human as an evaluation and oversight protocol, which is the debate paradigm.

assignments.note: 2021-04 Dynabench
assignments.why: Annotators write adversarial examples that fool the current model and these become the next round's test data, a dynamically evolving adversarial test set.

assignments.note: 2021-07 Evaluating large language models trained on code HumanEval
assignments.why: Introduces pass@k functional correctness by executing hidden unit tests, i.e. execution-based verification rather than a judge scoring outputs.

assignments.note: 2022-02 Jury learning
assignments.why: Models individual annotators and aggregates a chosen jury's simulated verdicts in place of a majority label, an aggregation of several raters' judgments.

assignments.note: 2022-02 Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
assignments.why: A red-team LM generates adversarial test inputs and is improved (few-shot from past hits, SFT, RL) to find more failures in the target.

assignments.note: 2022-03 Self-consistency improves chain of thought reasoning
assignments.why: Takes a majority vote over many sampled reasoning paths (aggregating outputs by a voting rule) and uses agreement rate as a consistency-based confidence check.

assignments.note: 2022-04 Single-turn debate does not help humans answer hard reading-comprehension questions
assignments.why: Tests single-turn debate arguments as an aid to human judges on QuALITY, a study of the debate paradigm.

assignments.note: 2022-05 AdaTest
assignments.why: An LLM proposes tests in a topic tree and the suite grows around the target model's failures, a generated test set that adapts to where the model fails.

assignments.note: 2022-07 CodeT code generation with generated tests
assignments.why: Ranks candidate code by dual execution agreement (execution-based verification) using tests the model itself generates (generated test sets).

assignments.note: 2022-07 Language models mostly know what they know
assignments.why: Its main subject is whether LM probabilities are calibrated and training P(IK), with measurement of calibration and self-evaluation behaviour (including degradation OOD and under RLHF) as the contribution.

assignments.note: 2022-10 Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
assignments.why: Studies how proxy reward models of varying size are overoptimised by BoN and PPO, i.e. RLHF-style reward models learned from preference labels.

assignments.note: 2022-10 Two-turn debate does not help humans answer hard reading comprehension questions
assignments.why: Tests whether a two-turn debate with rebuttal helps human judges, a study of the debate paradigm.

assignments.note: 2022-12 Discovering LM Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations
assignments.why: LMs generate 154 evaluation datasets filtered by a preference model, i.e. model-generated test sets.

assignments.note: 2022-12 Evaluating human-language model interaction
assignments.why: HALIE evaluates the interactive process and first-person user experience instead of a single score on outputs, showing non-interactive metrics fail to predict interactive quality.

assignments.note: 2023-02 Semantic uncertainty
assignments.why: Detects likely errors via consistency of meaning across sampled answers (semantic entropy), a sample-consistency check rather than a judge scoring one output.
A GPT-4 judge design with auto-CoT evaluation steps and probability-weighted form-filling scores for reference-free NLG grading.

assignments.note: 2023-03 SelfCheckGPT
assignments.why: Reference-free hallucination detection by checking each sentence's consistency against other sampled responses, a consistency-check method for judging outputs.

assignments.note: 2023-05 AlpacaFarm
assignments.why: Replaces human pairwise feedback with LLM annotators (the origin of AlpacaEval auto-evaluation) to simulate and study methods that learn from pairwise human feedback.

assignments.note: 2023-05 AttrScore Automatic Evaluation of Attribution
assignments.why: Prompted and fine-tuned LLMs judge whether a cited source supports a generated claim, covering both judge prompting and fine-tuned judges.

assignments.note: 2023-05 Encouraging divergent thinking through multi-agent debate
assignments.why: MAD framework with affirmative and negative debaters and a judge, a debate protocol.

assignments.note: 2023-05 EvalPlus Is your code generated by ChatGPT really correct
assignments.why: Execution-based differential testing of code with LLM-seeded and mutation-generated test inputs that expose insufficient original tests.

assignments.note: 2023-05 Improving factuality and reasoning through multiagent debate
assignments.why: Several LLM instances debate over rounds, reading and revising against each other's answers, the multi-agent debate paradigm.

assignments.note: 2023-05 LLMs are not Fair Evaluators
assignments.why: Measures that swapping answer order flips GPT-4/ChatGPT verdicts (audit, order sensitivity) and proposes balanced-position and multiple-evidence calibration to make the judge less biased.

assignments.note: 2023-05 LM vs LM detecting factual errors via cross examination
assignments.why: An examiner LM cross-examines an examinee LM and judges claims false from inconsistencies, a cross-examination protocol with an LLM as the judge.

assignments.note: 2023-05 Let's Verify Step by Step PRM800K
assignments.why: Trains process reward models on human step-level labels, shows they beat outcome reward models, and releases PRM800K.

assignments.note: 2023-05 Voyager
assignments.why: An automatic curriculum proposes new tasks from the agent's state and a self-verification module judges success, the propose-verify loop of generated tasks the note files it for.

assignments.note: 2023-06 Evaluating superhuman models with consistency checks
assignments.why: Evaluates via logical consistency rules instead of ground truth and measures violations (incoherent forecasts, chess evaluations, legal predictions) as the contribution.

assignments.note: 2023-06 Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
assignments.why: Studies GPT-4 as a judge (judging), measures its agreement and position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases (audit), introduces Chatbot Arena pairwise voting (arena), and measures position consistency under swap with swap-based fixes (order sensitivity).

assignments.note: 2023-06 Language-Model-as-an-Examiner
assignments.why: An LM examiner grades examinees and writes its own questions and follow-ups based on their answers, a judge design with generated, adaptive test items.

assignments.note: 2023-06 PandaLM
assignments.why: A fine-tuned 7B LLaMA pairwise judge trained on GPT-3.5 labels, whose subject is the judge itself.
